title: So Let Our Lips and Lives Express
description: So Let Our Lips and Lives Express in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 132, headed “Holiness and grace, Titus 2. 10-13”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: So let our lips and lives ex-press The ho-ly gos-pel we pro-fess, So let our works and vi-rtues shine To prove the doc-trine all di-vine.

lines: So let our lips and lives express
So let our works and virtues shine
To prove the doctrine all divine.
Thus shall we best proclaim abroad
The honours of our saviour God;
And grace subdues the power of sin.
Our flesh and sense must be deny'd,
Passion and envy, lust and pride;
While justice, temperance, truth and love
While we expect that blessed hope,
The bright appearance of the Lord,
And faith stands leaning on his word.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
